primitives.name: TBI should be studied at the systems neuroscience level, correlating neural circuitry changes with function
primitives.verbatim_quote: Much can be learned about TBI by studying this disorder on a systems neuroscience level and correlating changes in neural circuitry with neurological and cognitive function.
primitives.page: Front matter, Topic description, text lines 98-102
assumptions: Function is an emergent property of circuitry, not only of local tissue damage
Circuit changes can be measured and correlated with cognitive outcomes
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when circuit measures are unavailable and only lesion anatomy is recorded; correlation with function is not by itself a causal mechanism

layer2.mapping: A reasoning engine should model a performer or team as a network whose output depends on connections between units, not only on the state of individual units, and should score connection level changes against observed function.
layer2.telemetry: Circuit level measures, connectivity metrics, and paired functional outcome scores over time

primitives.name: Networks are disrupted and then reshaped after TBI, and tracking that reshaping is where treatment benefit lies
primitives.verbatim_quote: Further progress in understanding the disruption and subsequent reshaping of networks is likely to have substantial benefits in the treatment of patients with TBI-associated deficits.
primitives.page: Front matter, Topic description, text lines 115-117
assumptions: Post injury network change is dynamic rather than a fixed deficit
Tools for measuring assemblies and networks keep improving
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down at a single time point snapshot; reshaping cannot be inferred without longitudinal measurement

layer2.mapping: Engine state should be time varying: after a shock, model a disruption phase and a separate reshaping phase with different parameters, instead of applying one permanent downgrade.
layer2.telemetry: Repeated network measures at multiple post shock time points, plus functional outcomes at the same times

primitives.name: The Topic includes treatment options for TBI patients that modulate network function
primitives.verbatim_quote: We also include articles on treatment options for TBI patients that modulate network function.
primitives.page: Front matter, Topic statement, text lines 124-131
assumptions: Synaptic, oscillatory, and connectivity measures tap the same underlying network dysfunction
Mechanisms at the cellular level propagate to network level function
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when one level is measured in isolation; a synaptic change without a network readout does not establish a functional deficit

layer2.mapping: Signals should be organized in three stacked families, local interaction strength, rhythm and timing, and long range connectivity, and a conclusion should require agreement across at least two families before it is treated as structural.
layer2.telemetry: Synaptic measures, oscillation spectra, and functional connectivity estimates for the same system

primitives.name: Systems neuroscience examines neural circuit activity and how it relates to behavior and function
primitives.verbatim_quote: Systems neuroscience examines the activity of neural circuits and how they relate to behavior and function.
primitives.page: Editorial, Chen, Burke and Cohen 2016, text lines 235-236
assumptions: Circuit activity is the level at which behavior is generated
TBI is therefore legible as a circuit disorder
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down for deficits driven mainly by non circuit factors such as systemic illness or peripheral injury

layer2.mapping: The engine should keep an explicit circuit layer between raw inputs and predicted behavior, so explanations cite which connection or rhythm changed rather than only which input moved.
layer2.telemetry: Circuit activity recordings, connectivity estimates, and behavioral measures collected in parallel

primitives.name: Upwards of 15 percent of mild TBI patients experience persistent symptoms
primitives.verbatim_quote: In patients with mild TBI's, upwards of 15% of patients experience persistent symptoms
primitives.page: Editorial, Chen, Burke and Cohen 2016, text lines 248-249
assumptions: The cited cohort generalizes to mild TBI populations broadly
Persistent symptoms are circuit mediated rather than only psychological
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down across case mixes; rates differ by setting, definition of persistence, and follow up interval

layer2.mapping: Base rates matter: a reasoning engine should carry an explicit persistence base rate for post shock symptoms instead of treating every shock as either fully resolved or permanently damaging.
layer2.telemetry: Cohort follow up rates, symptom persistence proportions, and time since injury

primitives.name: A systems biology approach is the appropriate framework for quantitative neuroimaging findings in TBI
primitives.verbatim_quote: This review argues that a systems biology approach to understanding quantitative neuroimaging findings in TBI provides an appropriate framework for better utilizing the information derived from quantitative neuroimaging and its relation with neuropsychological outcome.
primitives.page: Bigler 2016, Abstract, text lines 385-388
assumptions: Quantitative image features carry information that qualitative reads discard
Imaging levels from tissue to whole person form one system
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when quantification is uncalibrated across scanners or when outcome measures are too coarse to register network change

layer2.mapping: Replace qualitative labels with quantitative features wherever a measurement exists, and relate those features to outcomes inside one multilevel model rather than as isolated facts.
layer2.telemetry: Automated image quantification outputs, volumetric and diffusion metrics, and standardized outcome scores

primitives.name: A single Glasgow Coma Scale level hides a wide disparity of structural pathology
primitives.verbatim_quote: The problem of traumatic brain injury (TBI) severity classification by using the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) is the wide disparity of structural pathology that may be present for a given classification level.
primitives.page: Bigler 2016, Figure 1 caption, text lines 496-497
assumptions: Cases shown span the GCS range with and without visible abnormality
Structural pathology is the relevant hidden variable behind the score
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down as a complete severity account; GCS still carries prognostic value, it is the one number summary that fails

layer2.mapping: Any single summary rating in the engine should be treated as a compression with known hidden variance: two cases with the same rating can carry opposite structural states, so the rating must never veto contradictory structural evidence.
layer2.telemetry: Distributions of structural findings conditioned on each rating level, not only the rating itself

primitives.name: Impact energy translates forward and opposite, so the greatest damage can sit away from the impact point
primitives.verbatim_quote: Some of the energy of that impact becomes translated forward and opposite (contrecoup) resulting in multiple areas of surface contusion and hemorrhagic shear injury in the left frontal (top yellow arrow) and temporal lobe regions (bottom yellow arrow in the upper left CT).
primitives.page: Bigler 2016, Figure 3 caption, text lines 616-629
assumptions: Biomechanical deformation follows the direction of brain displacement
Shear strain concentrates where tissue properties change
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down for purely focal penetrating injury and for slow loading where inertial shear is minimal

layer2.mapping: Shock propagation in a network is not local: the largest downstream effect can appear at the node opposite or most mechanically mismatched to the entry point, so impact analysis must trace transfer paths rather than only inspecting the entry node.
layer2.telemetry: Impact direction, tissue strain maps, and lesion location relative to impact site

primitives.name: Volume loss mapped against a normative template projects which dependent networks are affected
primitives.verbatim_quote: Assuming that where significant volume reduction has occurred would reflect damage to networks dependent on those areas, a schematic network map from Cole et al. (2013) is used to project where damage is and what networks would be affected.
primitives.page: Bigler 2016, Figure 11 caption, text lines 1072-1076
assumptions: The normative template is an appropriate reference for the individual
Network membership of a region predicts functional consequence of its loss
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when individual anatomy departs strongly from the template or when plasticity has remapped network membership

layer2.mapping: Maintain a normative reference distribution for every tracked unit, express each case as a deviation map against that reference, and propagate deviations through a dependency map to forecast which downstream functions degrade.
layer2.telemetry: Individual deviation maps against normative samples, plus a region to network dependency table

primitives.name: Scan sequences can be mined for structural, diffusion, and functional metrics for comparison against a normative sample
primitives.verbatim_quote: the different types of scans and scan sequences can be mined for structural, DTI and functional imaging metrics so that individual comparisons can be made within each data point in reference to a normative sample
primitives.page: Bigler 2016, Figure 12 caption, text lines 1239-1248
assumptions: Different sequences tap different levels of the same pathology
A shared normative dataset makes individual comparison interpretable
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when normative samples are small, demographically mismatched, or collected on different protocols

layer2.mapping: Every engine feature should be stored with its normative distribution so a new observation is read as a percentile or deviation, not as a raw number without context.
layer2.telemetry: Feature level normative means and spreads, case level deviations, and protocol identifiers

primitives.name: Axonal injury is an injury to the substrate by which brain networks communicate
primitives.verbatim_quote: Unlike focal injury to a discrete brain region, axonal injury is fundamentally an injury to the substrate by which networks of the brain communicate with one another.
primitives.page: Wolf and Koch 2016, Abstract, text lines 1567-1569
assumptions: White matter axons are preferentially vulnerable to biomechanical forces
Network communication depends on the integrity of long axonal conduits
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down for purely focal cortical lesions where the deficit is local computation loss rather than disconnection

layer2.mapping: Distinguish node damage from edge damage in the engine: a system can lose function because a unit failed or because the links between healthy units failed, and the two failures predict different recovery patterns.
layer2.telemetry: White matter integrity measures, tract level damage maps, and node level function measures

primitives.name: Traumatic axonal injury disrupts the timing of neuronal communication, underlying cognitive dysfunction
primitives.verbatim_quote: Our central hypothesis is that traumatic injury to axons may disrupt the exquisite timing of neuronal communication within and between brain networks, and that this may underlie aspects of post-TBI cognitive dysfunction.
primitives.page: Wolf and Koch 2016, Abstract, text lines 1573-1575
assumptions: Ensemble coding is timing dependent
Axonal conduction delays are a plausible causal route from injury to cognition
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down where amplitude or rate coding dominates and timing precision is not load bearing for the task

layer2.mapping: Add timing as a first class signal: not only whether units are active, but whether their activity arrives in the right order and phase, since a network with intact units and broken timing still fails.
layer2.telemetry: Inter regional latency, phase coherence, and ensemble synchrony measures before and after injury

primitives.name: Axonal injury causes loss or derangement of synchronization within intra-hippocampal connections
primitives.verbatim_quote: TBI induced axonal injury results in loss of, or derangement in
primitives.page: Wolf and Koch 2016, summary points, text lines 2113-2141
assumptions: Hippocampal oscillatory function depends on intra-hippocampal synchrony
Memory construction ensembles are the downstream casualty
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when compensatory pathways restore synchrony or when the measured rhythm is not the one the task uses

layer2.mapping: Local synchrony inside a subsystem should be monitored separately from global activity: a subsystem can look active while its internal coordination, and therefore its output quality, has collapsed.
layer2.telemetry: Within region coherence, ensemble formation rates, and memory task performance

primitives.name: Changes in sensory processing are a significant contributor to post TBI cognitive and motor deficits
primitives.verbatim_quote: we have hypothesized that a significant contributor to the cognitive and motor deficits seen after TBI could be changes in sensory processing.
primitives.page: Carron, Alwis and Rajan 2016, Abstract, text lines 2516-2518
assumptions: Interior and exterior life depends on responsiveness to information about the world
The whisker barrel system is a valid model test system for cortical sensory encoding
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down for deficits with no sensory component and when animal model encoding changes do not transfer to human cortex

layer2.mapping: Input processing quality is a hidden variable in any prediction system: if the sensing layer distorts its inputs, downstream reasoning inherits the distortion, so sensor layer fidelity should be measured directly.
layer2.telemetry: Sensory evoked response fidelity, encoding accuracy for simple and complex inputs, and downstream task scores

primitives.name: Common TBI produces persistent neuronal hyperexcitation in upper cortical layers, likely from changes in inhibition
primitives.verbatim_quote: form of TBI results in persistent neuronal hyperexcitation specifically in the upper
primitives.page: Carron, Alwis and Rajan 2016, Abstract, text lines 2528-2531
assumptions: Barrel cortex recordings represent cortical encoding generally
Layer specific effects can be separated from whole cortex averages
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down in deeper layers and in injury types where suppression rather than hyperexcitation dominates, especially acutely

layer2.mapping: Averages hide layer specific failure: track subsystems separately, because one layer can be hyperexcitable while another is suppressed, and a pooled signal would wrongly read as normal.
layer2.telemetry: Layer resolved activity measures, inhibitory neuron counts by type, and evoked response amplitudes over time

primitives.name: Changes in inhibition are a major change modulating the excitation inhibition balance in the long term TBI brain
primitives.verbatim_quote: appear to be one of the major changes modulating the E:I balance
primitives.page: Carron, Alwis and Rajan 2016, Conclusions, text lines 3146-3203
assumptions: Excitatory activity and connectivity are enhanced while inhibition is compromised after trauma
The supragranular layers show the most uniform cortical change
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down in subcortical regions where some areas increase inhibition as compensation, so one global balance shift does not hold

layer2.mapping: Balance variables need a sign and a region: the engine should represent excitation and inhibition as separate channels whose ratio is tracked per subsystem, since the same injury can push the ratio opposite ways in different places.
layer2.telemetry: Excitatory and inhibitory activity estimates per region, interneuron population measures, and ratio time series

primitives.name: Electrophysiology can track the temporal evolution of neuronal functionality changes with high precision
primitives.verbatim_quote: to provide the high-precision information needed to monitor and understand the
primitives.page: Carron, Alwis and Rajan 2016, electrophysiology discussion, text lines 3226-3266
assumptions: Non invasive extra cranial recording is portable and can be done at the bedside
Evoked activity is consistently altered in TBI, differently over time and by injury type
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down as a stand alone diagnostic; quantitative EEG alone showed limited diagnostic utility for mild TBI

layer2.mapping: Cheap, repeatable, high frequency measurement beats rare expensive measurement for tracking a changing system: the engine should prefer a dense time series of a good proxy over a single precise snapshot.
layer2.telemetry: Repeated EEG or evoked potential measures, approximate entropy, and band power ratios over the recovery course

primitives.name: The Slow Wave Coefficient is the ratio of summed delta plus theta power to summed alpha plus beta power
primitives.verbatim_quote: (the ratio of the summed power in the delta and theta bands
primitives.page: Carron, Alwis and Rajan 2016, electrophysiology discussion, text lines 3226-3266

symbol_and_unit_ledger.P_delta, P_theta: summed EEG power in the delta and theta bands, microvolts squared
symbol_and_unit_ledger.P_alpha, P_beta: summed EEG power in the alpha and beta bands, microvolts squared

assumptions: Band power sums are computed over the same EEG epoch
The ratio indexes unilateral TBI in the cited analysis
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down with artifacts, medication effects on band power, and sleep state changes that move the same bands

layer2.mapping: A ratio of low frequency to high frequency power is a compact state index: the engine can use analogous ratios, slow structural signal over fast surface signal, as a cheap continuous health gauge for a system.
layer2.telemetry: EEG band powers in delta, theta, alpha, and beta bands from the same recording epoch

primitives.name: Mitochondrial permeability transition pore opening after mild TBI is gated by cyclophilin-D
primitives.verbatim_quote: Mitochondria are central to cell survival and Ca2+ homeostasis due to their intracellular buffering capabilities. Mitochondrial dysfunction resulting in mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP) opening has been reported after mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI).
primitives.page: Sun and Jacobs 2016, Abstract, text lines 3670-3672
assumptions: Cyclosporine A protects against pore opening through its interaction with cyclophilin-D
Mitochondrial calcium buffering is central to cell survival
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when cell death proceeds through pore independent pathways or when injury severity overwhelms mitochondrial protection

layer2.mapping: Single gatekeeper components deserve explicit modeling: one regulator, here cyclophilin-D, can decide whether a stressed subsystem crosses into failure, so the engine should flag gatekeeper variables rather than averaging them into a general stress score.
layer2.telemetry: Mitochondrial calcium load, pore opening markers, and cell survival after injury

primitives.name: Total adaptation is the frequency of the first two action potentials divided by the frequency of the last two in a sweep
primitives.verbatim_quote: total adaptation = frequency of first two APs in the sweep divided by the frequency of the last two APs in the sweep
primitives.page: Sun and Jacobs 2016, Figure 4 caption, text lines 4065-4076

symbol_and_unit_ledger.f_first2: frequency of the first two action potentials in the sweep, hertz
symbol_and_unit_ledger.f_last2: frequency of the last two action potentials in the sweep, hertz

assumptions: Adaptation is measured within one 400 ms depolarizing sweep
First pair and last pair frequencies summarize the firing pattern change
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down for neurons firing fewer than four action potentials in a sweep and across different sweep durations

layer2.mapping: Within episode adaptation is a usable fatigue signature: compare early response rate to late response rate inside the same episode rather than comparing absolute rates across episodes.
layer2.telemetry: Action potential timestamps within a stimulation sweep, injected current level, and neuron class

primitives.name: Inhibiting cyclophilin-D after TBI reduces synaptic hyperexcitation and remains a treatment target
primitives.verbatim_quote: suggest that inhibiting CypD after TBI is an effective strategy to reduce synaptic
primitives.page: Sun and Jacobs 2016, Abstract, text lines 3702-3706
assumptions: Knockout results indicate the direction a pharmacological inhibitor should push
Protection was partial for intrinsic properties, so the target is one contributor among several
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down as a complete rescue claim; the knockout also changed membrane properties directly, confounding a purely selective interpretation

layer2.mapping: Interventions should be graded as partial by default: the engine should record which sub measures an intervention normalized, which it overshot, and which it left unchanged, instead of a single worked or failed verdict.
layer2.telemetry: Spontaneous and miniature EPSC frequency, action potential slope, rheobase, and input resistance by treatment group

primitives.name: TBI increases Drp1 driven mitochondrial fission, and inhibiting fission improves hippocampal learning and memory
primitives.verbatim_quote: inhibition of fission improves hippocampal-dependent learning and memory, suggesting
primitives.page: Fischer et al. 2016, Abstract, text lines 4587-4591
assumptions: Drp1 translocates to the mitochondrial outer membrane to initiate fission
Mitochondrial length distribution is a readout of the fusion fission balance
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down over time; length first increased at 24 hours before decreasing at 72 hours, so a single time point can invert the conclusion

layer2.mapping: Structure turnover balance is a state variable: when a system fragments faster than it reconnects, function degrades, and the fragmentation rate itself is measurable before output fails.
layer2.telemetry: Drp1 levels in mitochondrial fractions, mitochondrial length distributions, and newborn neuron survival counts

primitives.name: Post injury Mdivi-1 prevented the decrease in mitochondrial length and reduced loss of newborn hippocampal neurons
primitives.verbatim_quote: a pharmacological inhibitor of Drp1, prevented this decrease in mitochondria length.
primitives.page: Fischer et al. 2016, Abstract, text lines 4582-4586
assumptions: Treatment began after injury, so the window is post injury rather than prophylactic
Behavioral improvement tracks the structural rescue
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down outside the tested dosing schedule and in regions other than hippocampus that were not measured

layer2.mapping: Timing of intervention relative to a known trajectory inflection is decisive: the same intervention applied before the 72 hour fragmentation shift is a different intervention from one applied after it.
layer2.telemetry: Treatment start time, mitochondrial length at 24 and 72 hours, and memory task scores by treatment group

primitives.name: TBI upregulates hippocampal phosphodiesterase isoforms, a candidate mechanism for the fall in cAMP and impaired plasticity
primitives.verbatim_quote: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) results in significant impairments in hippocampal synaptic plasticity.
primitives.page: Wilson et al. 2016, Abstract, text lines 5302-5305
assumptions: Phosphodiesterases degrade cAMP, so their upregulation can explain lower cAMP
Isoform and time course specificity matters; only some isoforms changed
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down as a sole mechanism claim; expression change does not by itself prove activity change in the relevant compartment

layer2.mapping: When a key messenger falls, look for increased degradation, not only decreased production: the engine should model both the source and the sink of every important signal.
layer2.telemetry: Isoform level PDE expression at 30 minutes to 7 days, cAMP levels, and cell type localization

primitives.name: PDE4 inhibition with rolipram partially rescued basal transmission and converted decaying LTP into long lasting LTP
primitives.verbatim_quote: converted a decaying form of long-term potentiation (LTP) into long-lasting LTP.
primitives.page: Wilson et al. 2016, Abstract, text lines 5326-5327
assumptions: Hippocampal slices preserve the plasticity deficit ex vivo
Pan PDE4 inhibition is the tested intervention, not isoform selective inhibition
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down as a whole animal cognition claim; slice rescue does not establish behavioral rescue or a safe systemic dose

layer2.mapping: A decaying signal that can be converted to a durable one by blocking its degradation is a distinct failure class: the engine should separate failure to form a pattern from failure to maintain it, because the fixes differ.
layer2.telemetry: Field EPSP slopes, LTP decay curves, and treatment condition in slice experiments

primitives.name: Methionine metabolism through transmethylation generates SAM, the principal methyl donor for epigenetic regulation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Metabolism of methionine via the transmethylation pathway generates S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) that serves as the principal methyl
primitives.page: Dash et al. 2016, Abstract, text lines 6062-6065
assumptions: Methionine is essential and obtained from the diet
SAM supply couples nutrition and metabolism to gene regulation
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when plasma levels do not reflect brain tissue levels or when methyltransferase activity is limited by other factors

layer2.mapping: Resource supply chains reach regulatory layers: a fall in a basic input metabolite can change which genes are expressed, so the engine should trace supply shocks through to regulatory consequences, not stop at the supply level.
layer2.telemetry: Plasma methionine and SAM levels, methylation marks, and gene expression changes after injury

primitives.name: Under oxidative stress, homocysteine enters the transsulfuration pathway to generate protective glutathione
primitives.verbatim_quote: Under conditions of oxidative stress, homocysteine (which is derived from SAM) enters the transsulfuration pathway to generate glutathione, an important cytoprotective
primitives.page: Dash et al. 2016, Abstract, text lines 6068-6069
assumptions: The pathway choice depends on oxidative stress state
Glutathione is a key defense against oxidative damage, which TBI causes
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when precursor supply, cysteine and glycine, is itself depleted, as the same study found after severe TBI

layer2.mapping: Branching pathways create trade offs under stress: diverting a metabolite to defense removes it from regulation, so a stressed system pays for protection with reduced regulatory capacity, a cost the engine should book explicitly.
layer2.telemetry: Homocysteine routing, cysteine and glycine levels, glutathione levels, and oxidative stress markers

primitives.name: Decreased methionine and its products likely alter cellular function in multiple organs at a systems level
primitives.verbatim_quote: Taken together, these results suggest that decreased levels of methionine and its metabolic products are likely to alter cellular function in multiple organs at a systems level.
primitives.page: Dash et al. 2016, concluding abstract statement, text lines 6115-6117
assumptions: Plasma metabolite changes were graded by injury severity, stronger in severe than mild TBI
Methionine products serve many cellular functions across organs
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down as organ specific proof; plasma measurement shows association, not which organ functions changed

layer2.mapping: A brain injury with whole body metabolic signatures warns against local only models: the engine should check whether a local shock has systemic correlates before treating the system as closed.
layer2.telemetry: Multi organ metabolite panels, severity graded metabolite changes, and organ function measures

primitives.name: TBI alters physiological oscillatory rhythms, and low frequency septohippocampal stimulation entrained oscillations and improved spatial learning
primitives.verbatim_quote: Specifically, stimulation of the septohippocampal circuit in the theta frequency entrained oscillations and improved spatial learning following TBI.
primitives.page: Pevzner et al. 2016, Abstract, text lines 6638-6639
assumptions: Theta rhythm supports spatial learning circuitry
Entrainment by external stimulation can substitute for a lost endogenous rhythm
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down outside the theta band and the septohippocampal circuit; other circuits have other governing rhythms

layer2.mapping: A broken rhythm can be repaired by pacing: if a subsystem has lost its timing signal, an external pacemaker at the natural frequency is a candidate fix, and its success is measurable as entrainment plus functional gain.
layer2.telemetry: Oscillation spectra, stimulation frequency, entrainment measures, and spatial learning scores

primitives.name: Electrical neuromodulation is a candidate therapy because TBI altered rhythms are measurable and stimulable
primitives.verbatim_quote: Electrical neuromodulation is one approach that has shown promise in alleviating symptoms associated with neurological disorders such as in Parkinson's disease (PD) and epilepsy.
primitives.page: Pevzner et al. 2016, Abstract, text lines 6633-6635
assumptions: Neuromodulation has precedent in other neurological disorders
Clinical translation needs hypothesis driven preclinical design
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when stimulation parameters, target, or timing are extrapolated across disorders without circuit specific testing

layer2.mapping: Borrow interventions only with their mechanism attached: a therapy that works by restoring rhythm in one disorder is a candidate for another disorder only where the same rhythm failure is documented.
layer2.telemetry: Stimulation target and parameters, disorder specific rhythm findings, and outcome measures

primitives.name: Cognitive dysfunction after mild TBI relates to subtle physiological changes in the hippocampus despite no overt defects
primitives.verbatim_quote: There is increasing evidence that cognitive and memory dysfunction is related to subtle physiological changes that occur in the hippocampus, and these impact both the phenotype of deficits observed and subsequent recovery.
primitives.page: Girgis et al. 2016, Abstract, text lines 7837-7839
assumptions: Mild TBI is defined by absence of major imaging or histopathological defects
Physiological change can exist below imaging resolution
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when a normal physiological workup accompanies persistent deficits, implicating other regions or network level causes

layer2.mapping: Absence of visible damage is not absence of damage: the engine should keep a sub resolution failure class for cases where output is impaired but structural measures are clean, and route those cases to functional measurement.
layer2.telemetry: Hippocampal physiology measures, cognitive testing, and imaging findings in the same patients

primitives.name: Medications used for other indications or brain stimulation may modulate post mTBI hippocampal activity therapeutically
primitives.verbatim_quote: Therapeutic modulation of physiological activity by means of medications commonly used for other indications or brain stimulation may represent novel treatment approaches.
primitives.page: Girgis et al. 2016, Abstract, text lines 7840-7842
assumptions: Known drugs have known safety profiles, shortening translation
The target is physiological activity, not structural repair
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when the repurposed drug's primary effect harms another injured system or when stimulation targets are wrong

layer2.mapping: Repurposing is a search strategy: before inventing a new intervention, scan known interventions whose mechanism matches the documented failure, including interventions built for other problems.
layer2.telemetry: Drug mechanism profiles, hippocampal activity measures, and cognitive outcomes

primitives.name: mTBI changes stimulation evoked cerebral blood flow responses in sensorimotor cortex, marking altered neurovascular activity
primitives.verbatim_quote: we demonstrate post-traumatic changes in cerebral blood flow (CBF) in the sensorimotor cortex in response to whisker stimulation compared to sham using functional Laser Doppler Imaging (fLDI) at adulthood (P67-P73).
primitives.page: Murugan et al. 2016, Abstract, text lines 8525-8528
assumptions: Developing rats injured at P25-P26 were measured at adulthood, so the signature is persistent
Blood flow response is a proxy for underlying neuronal activity
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when vascular injury itself, rather than neuronal activity change, drives the blood flow signature

layer2.mapping: Proxy signals must be validated against the thing they proxy: a blood flow change can mean neuronal change or vascular change, and the engine should keep both readings alive until a discriminating measure arrives.
layer2.telemetry: Evoked CBF response maps, neuronal activity measures, and behavioral scores in the same animals

primitives.name: Facilitating mitochondrial calcium uptake with kaempferol improved neurovascular activity and sensorimotor behavior after mTBI
primitives.verbatim_quote: facilitation of mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake in the early window after injury may sustain
primitives.page: Murugan et al. 2016, Abstract, text lines 8552-8558
assumptions: Surviving neurons had diminished mitochondrial calcium influx and oxidative metabolism
Treatment was given in the early window after injury
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down for the lost neuronal population; kaempferol did not augment or restore neuronal loss, it improved function of survivors

layer2.mapping: Support the survivors is a distinct strategy from replacing the lost: after attrition, raising the capacity of remaining units can recover system output, and the engine should model survivor capacity as a lever separate from unit count.
layer2.telemetry: Mitochondrial calcium uptake, oxidative metabolism, neuronal survival counts, and behavior after treatment

primitives.name: mTOR signaling links post injury neurogenesis and mossy fiber sprouting to post traumatic epileptogenesis
primitives.verbatim_quote: A prominent cell signaling pathway activated in animal models of both TBI and epilepsy is the mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR).
primitives.page: Butler et al. 2015, Abstract, text lines 9257-9258
assumptions: Adult neurogenesis increases shortly after TBI in the dentate gyrus
Newborn neurons and sprouting can integrate into recurrent excitatory circuits
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down as a universal epilepsy mechanism; post traumatic epilepsy also arises from neocortical injury without dentate involvement

layer2.mapping: Growth after damage is double edged: repair processes that add new units and connections can also wire in pathological feedback loops, so the engine should score post shock growth for both recovery value and loop formation risk.
layer2.telemetry: Doublecortin labeling, mossy fiber sprouting measures, recurrent excitation, and seizure prevalence

primitives.name: Rapamycin attenuated mossy fiber sprouting and recurrent excitation and diminished seizure prevalence after CCI
primitives.verbatim_quote: At later times post-injury (8-13 weeks), evidence of mossy fiber sprouting and increased
primitives.page: Butler et al. 2015, Abstract, text lines 9278-9283
assumptions: Rapamycin was given daily from the day of injury until tissue collection
Rapamycin reduced post traumatic neurogenesis but did not prevent cell loss
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down as a cell survival claim and outside the controlled cortical impact model and dosing used here

layer2.mapping: Suppressing a growth pathway trades repair for stability: the engine should represent such interventions as a trade with two scored outcomes, less pathological reorganization against less regenerative growth.
layer2.telemetry: Sprouting and excitability measures at 8 to 13 weeks, seizure prevalence, and cell loss stains by treatment

reasoning_traces.think: This edited volume is a research topic, not a single experiment, and its value is the way it forces one question at several levels at once: what happens to a network when its parts are injured, and which level of description actually explains the lost function. The editors open by conceding the traditional view, in which traumatic brain injury is an anatomic and neuropathological condition managed by defining a lesion and limiting secondary damage, and then argue that this view pays too little attention to the function of the organ. Their alternative is to study the disorder at the systems neuroscience level, correlating changes in neural circuitry with neurological and cognitive function. That framing runs through all eleven contributions and gives the collection a coherence that edited volumes often lack. The first section sets governing principles. Bigler shows that clinical neuroimaging is usually read qualitatively even though automated quantification can extract far more, and that a systems biology frame, tissue to organ to whole person, is what lets quantitative imaging speak to neuropsychological outcome. His figure captions carry some of the sharpest claims in the book: a Glasgow Coma Scale level conceals a wide disparity of structural pathology, impact energy translates to a contrecoup site opposite the blow, and Jacobian warping against a normative template turns volume loss into a projection of which networks will fail. Wolf and Koch then supply the volume's central hypothesis, that axonal injury is an injury to the communication substrate itself and that its cognitive cost is paid in timing, because ensembles encode information in ways that depend on precise synchrony within and between networks. Carron and colleagues ground the same idea in sensory cortex, where the most common form of injury produces persistent hyperexcitation in upper layers, attributed to changed inhibition, so that the excitation to inhibition balance shifts and neuronal encoding of naturalistic input is distorted. The second section descends to the cellular machinery that network activity is built from, and it is strikingly mitochondrial. Sun and Jacobs use cyclophilin-D knockout mice to show that blocking permeability transition pore opening ameliorates excitatory synaptic abnormalities and partly normalizes intrinsic firing properties after mild injury, while leaving some properties changed or even reversed, which makes the protection real but partial and mechanistically mixed. Fischer and colleagues show a time dependent mitochondrial dynamics story, length first up at twenty four hours and fission dominant by seventy two, with Drp1 increased in mitochondrial fractions and its inhibitor Mdivi-1 preserving length, newborn neurons, and memory. Wilson and colleagues work the signaling layer, finding specific phosphodiesterase isoforms upregulated on distinct time courses after injury, degrading the cAMP that hippocampal plasticity needs, with rolipram converting a decaying potentiation into a lasting one in slices. Dash and colleagues widen the lens to the whole body, showing plasma methionine and its transmethylation and transsulfuration products falling after human injury in a severity graded way, which ties a dietary amino acid supply chain to epigenetic regulation and antioxidant defense at a systems level. The third section returns to networks with therapies aimed at circuit function. Pevzner and colleagues review oscillations and argue that entraining the septohippocampal circuit at theta frequency restored rhythms and spatial learning, making electrical neuromodulation a rational candidate rather than a speculative one. Girgis and colleagues survey hippocampal physiological change after mild injury, where there is no overt structural defect to treat, and propose repurposed medications and stimulation aimed at activity itself. Murugan and colleagues show that facilitating mitochondrial calcium uptake with kaempferol in the early window normalized evoked cerebral blood flow responses and improved behavior in surviving populations, joining the mitochondrial and network stories in one result. Butler and colleagues close with the dark side of plasticity: mTOR driven neurogenesis and mossy fiber sprouting after cortical impact build recurrent excitation and seizures, and rapamycin attenuates the reorganization and the epilepsy at the cost of the growth itself. Read together, the volume teaches a method as much as a set of facts. Measure quantitatively against normative references. Separate node damage from connection damage. Track timing and balance, not only activity levels. Expect interventions to be partial, time window dependent, and traded against something else. And expect the same injury to look different at every level, which is exactly why a reasoning engine needs all the levels wired into one account rather than a pile of independent signals. Two further lessons deserve emphasis because they are easy to miss. The first is heterogeneity as a design constraint rather than a nuisance. The editorial stresses that pinpointing the network cause of a specific symptom is hard precisely because injuries and symptoms vary across patients, and Bigler's case study method answers that problem directly, extracting from one deeply imaged child the kind of trajectory information that group averages wash out. A reasoning engine built on this work therefore needs a case level mode, in which one well measured instance can generate hypotheses that group data later tests, instead of a population only mode that discards outliers as noise. The second lesson is that assessment has to change when measurement changes. Bigler notes that paper and pencil neuropsychology was built for a non digital era and is poorly matched to network analysis, and Carron's group argues the same for electrophysiology, which remains underused clinically despite being portable, cheap, and repeatable at the bedside. Instruments define what a field can see, so an engine should periodically audit its own instruments, asking which of its measures are legacy conveniences and which actually tap the level where the failure lives. That audit, the normative comparisons, the timing measures, and the balance ratios together form the volume's practical bequest.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The lineage of this work runs from classical lesion neurology and the Glasgow Coma Scale era of severity grading, through the diffuse axonal injury pathology established in the early nineteen eighties, into the connectome period in which the brain is described as interconnected networks communicating over long axonal conduits. Systems biology supplied the multilevel template that Bigler imports into neuroimaging, borrowing the tissue to organ to organism pyramid and its demand for normative databases. The oscillation and entrainment material descends from decades of hippocampal theta and sharp wave ripple research, while the mitochondrial chapters descend from cell death biology, permeability transition, and fission fusion dynamics worked out outside brain injury and then carried into it. The editors' contribution is genealogical as much as scientific: they place these separate ancestries under one research topic heading and declare them one problem.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The editors and contributors share a model of the reader as a clinician scientist who already accepts molecular and cellular accounts and needs persuading that those accounts are incomplete rather than wrong. Their model of the domain is that function lives at the circuit level, that the circuit level is measurable with imaging, electrophysiology, and behavior in parallel, and that heterogeneity across patients is the central obstacle, because dissimilar injuries converge on similar symptoms through different network routes. They assume the reader will accept animal model circuitry, especially rodent hippocampus and barrel cortex, as evidence about human network principles, and they write therapeutically throughout: nearly every mechanism chapter ends by naming a target, a stimulation site, or a repurposed drug, because their model of the field's purpose is intervention, not description alone.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Several findings in this volume veto comfortable moves elsewhere. The Glasgow Coma Scale disparity vetoes any severity judgment made from one summary score when structural evidence disagrees. The timing hypothesis vetoes amplitude only accounts of network health, since intact units with deranged synchrony still fail. The regional split in inhibition, excitation up in cortex and suppression up in parts of hippocampus, vetoes any single global excitation inhibition shift applied to the whole brain. The partial and overshooting rescue in the cyclophilin-D knockout vetoes binary intervention verdicts. The rapamycin result vetoes treating post injury growth as purely good, and the methionine data veto closed system models of a brain only injury. Any layer built on this work must let these constraints override smoother stories.

universal_lens: Any complex system that fails by disconnection rather than by destruction needs this template: measure the parts quantitatively against a normative reference, measure the connections and their timing separately, track balance variables per subsystem rather than globally, and judge every intervention as partial, timed, and traded against another function. The pattern transfers to organizations, infrastructure, and software systems, where a single summary score hides structural disparity in exactly the way a coma scale hides lesion disparity, and where post shock regrowth can wire in pathological feedback just as sprouting wires in seizures.
gsi_mapping: The Galaxy Sports Institute takes from this volume a research method for studying injured and recovering performers: normative referenced quantitative measurement instead of qualitative labels, layer resolved tracking instead of pooled averages, explicit persistence base rates after a shock, and a standing distinction between node failure, connection failure, and timing failure. Its study designs should pair structural, functional, and outcome measures in the same subjects over time, grade interventions by which sub measures they normalize, and treat post injury adaptation as a trade that can help or harm.
gse_mapping: The Galaxy Sports Edge reasoning engine takes a network model of performance: units and the links between them are separate state variables, timing and synchrony are first class signals, excitation and inhibition style balance ratios are tracked per subsystem, and every observation is read as a deviation from a normative distribution. Shocks propagate to non local nodes, recovery follows a disruption then reshaping trajectory, and interventions or returns from absence are scored as partial and time window dependent. None of this is betting content; it is the engine's general machinery for reasoning about damaged and recovering systems.
